name: Vector3int16
simple: Vector3int16 is like a Vector3 (X, Y, Z), but each number must be a WHOLE number between -32,768 and 32,767. It saves memory, but it has no handy tools like Magnitude or Unit. Most games never need it; you will usually use Vector3 instead.
analogy: If Vector3 is a ruler that can measure tiny fractions, Vector3int16 is a ruler that only has whole-number marks and stops at 32,767.
whenToUse: When a Roblox feature specifically asks for one, for example building a Region3int16 (a box of whole-number spots used by some Terrain tools).
Almost never otherwise; use Vector3 for positions, sizes and directions.
where: Built-in data type, works in Scripts and LocalScripts. Make one with `Vector3int16.new(x, y, z)`.

terms.integer: A whole number with no decimal part, like 3 or -40 (not 2.5).
terms.16-bit signed integer: A whole number stored in a small box of memory. It can only hold numbers from -32,768 to 32,767, and can be negative (that is what "signed" means).
terms.overflow: When a number is too big for its box and wraps around to the other end. Putting 32,768 into a 16-bit integer turns it into -32,768, like a car odometer rolling over.
terms.rounded down: Decimal parts are thrown away so you get a whole number, for example 3.9 becomes 3.
terms.component: One of the numbers inside the vector, like X or Y.

examples.title: Make one and turn it into a normal Vector3
examples.code:
local small = Vector3int16.new(1, 2, 3)
print(small.X, small.Y, small.Z) --> 1 2 3

-- Convert by passing each number separately
local normal = Vector3.new(small.X, small.Y, small.Z)
print(normal) --> 1, 2, 3
explain: To use it with Vector3 tools, copy each number into `Vector3.new` one by one.

gotchas: Do NOT write `Vector3.new(myVector3int16)`. It silently gives (0, 0, 0) with no error. Pass `.X, .Y, .Z` separately.
Numbers past 32,767 wrap around to big negative numbers (overflow). Keep values in range, including after math.

Vector3int16.new.simple: Makes a new Vector3int16 from three whole numbers. Decimal parts are rounded down. Each number must be from -32,768 to 32,767.
Vector3int16.new.example:
local v = Vector3int16.new(10, 20.7, 30)
print(v.Y) --> 20  (the .7 was dropped)
Vector3int16.new.gotcha: 32,768 is one too big and wraps around to -32,768.

Vector3int16.X.simple: The X whole number. Lowercase `.x` also works.

Vector3int16.Y.simple: The Y whole number. Lowercase `.y` also works.

Vector3int16.Z.simple: The Z whole number. Lowercase `.z` also works.

op:Vector3int16+Vector3int16.gotcha: If a total goes past 32,767 it wraps around (overflow).

op:Vector3int16*Vector3int16.gotcha: Products get big fast; stay under 32,767.

op:Vector3int16/Vector3int16.simple: Divides matching numbers. The answers are rounded down to whole numbers.

op:Vector3int16*number.simple: Multiplies every number by the same amount. `number * Vector3int16` works too.

op:Vector3int16/number.simple: Divides every number by the same amount. The answers are rounded toward zero (decimals dropped).
